annotations.note: The cited study never defines stigma; it only lists manifestations (e.g. 'prejudice (devaluation of HCWs)') that it attributes to its own references [7, 8]. The general definition is not in the cited work.
The cited interview study says stigma 'still poses a threat to mental well-being' of hospital doctors. Doctors are healthcare workers; flagging the claim as broader than the source is pedantic.
The cited Jordanian survey of depression and anxiety never mentions stigma (no occurrence in the full text), so it cannot support 'stigmatization can impact the mental health of HCWs'.

The cited work reports (citing another study) that perceived stigma is associated with anxiety and depression; PTSD and suicide are absent, but the sentence cites two works [10, 11] for that list, and 'can lead to' over an association is a mild overstatement.
